What makes Diplodocus so amazing?

With its neck and tail making up most of its body, the Diplodocus was a long, slender, giant plant-eating dinosaur. Its whip-like tail, as long as 14 m, was one of its signature features.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Diplodocus

Diplodocus was about 24–27 m long, with its neck and tail longer than its trunk. Research has explored the possibility that it swung its 14 m tail — made of more than 80 bones — like a whip. It stripped plants with its comb-shaped teeth that were clustered only at the front, swallowed them whole, then digested them with gastroliths. Its neck bones were hollow and light with air sacs, and after hatching it grew to adult size in just 10 years.

Points worth exploring together

Point out details like the long neck and tail, the 14 m tail (whip), the comb-shaped teeth, and the fast growth. It's fun to talk about it together: "What do Diplodocus and Apatosaurus have in common?"

Parent guide — how to grow curiosity

Compare photos with Apatosaurus and look for what's alike and what's different. Observe together "Its teeth look like a comb!", and comparing its fast growth (10 years) with your child's own growth makes it fascinating.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How long was Diplodocus's tail?
A. About 14 m, made of more than 80 bones. Research has explored the possibility that it was swung like a whip.

Q. How did it eat?
A. It stripped plants with the comb-shaped teeth at the front, swallowed them whole, then digested them with gastroliths (stones).

Q. How can we enjoy this at home?
A. Compare it with Apatosaurus, observe the comb-shaped teeth, and talk about its fast growth.
